rounds.text: Shivagrico Implements Ltd trades at a price-to-book ratio of just 1.4x, which compares favourably against a sector benchmark of 2.63x [E7]. This low relative multiple is further supported by an absolute price-to-book of 1.45x, with shares trading at ₹ 24.0 against a book value of ₹ 16.5 [E2]. Furthermore, the company is actively investing in its future productive capacity, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) surging by 552.4% to reach ₹ 1.37 Cr in March 2026 [E40]. Conceded: the company delivers a poor five-year sales growth of 4.67% [E60], an ROA of 1.38% lagging the sector benchmark of 4.93% [E8], and a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4].

Shivagrico Implements Ltd carries an expensive valuation coupled with weak foundational performance metrics that fail to justify its pricing. Top-line expansion is severely sluggish, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of only 5% over 5 years [E15] that lags far behind the sector median sales growth of 18.7% [E75], alongside recent negative signals including a 3% year-over-year sales decline and decelerating earnings growth [E69, E70]. Furthermore, shareholders receive no cash return on their investment, as demonstrated by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], and the stock languishes low in its yearly range at only 29% of the way up its 52-week high [E5]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio is 1.45x on a book value of 16.5 against a sector benchmark of 2.63x [E2, E7], and capital work-in-progress (CWIP) has risen by 552.4% to reach ₹ 1.37 Cr [E40], indicating that growth spending is actively underway.

The bear overlooks the significant positive signal of acceleration in top-line expansion, where compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reaches 10% [E17]. While the bear points to sluggish 5-year sales [E15], profit growth recently exceeds 1-year price growth by 68% with a ratio of 35.00, demonstrating that the company is starting to outperform expectations [E56]. Conceded: dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], the stock sits at 29% of its 52-week range [E5], and 5-year sales growth is 5% [E15]. However, the massive 552.4% surge in Capital Work-in-Progress to ₹ 1.37 Cr shows a vital growth spend underway [E40], directly validating the company's asset deployment. Furthermore, valuation remains compelling as the price-to-book ratio of 1.4x (or 1.45x) trades at a deep discount to the sector benchmark of 2.63x [E2, E7].

The bull highlights a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 10% [E17], but this is undermined by a direct quarterly contraction with sales dropping 3% year-over-year [E69] and an overall earnings growth trajectory that is actively decelerating [E70]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio of 1.4x trades below the sector benchmark of 2.63x [E7], but this discount is entirely justified by a feeble return on assets of just 1.38% which severely lags the sector benchmark of 4.93% [E8]. While the bull points to a 552.4% surge in Capital Work-in-Progress to ₹ 1.37 Cr as a vital growth spend [E40], this massive capex build-up phase has yet to translate into meaningful top-line delivery given that long-term compounded sales growth stubbornly lingers at 5% to 6% [E14, E15, E16]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on profit growth outpacing 1-year price growth [E56] ignores the structural reality of poor five-year sales growth flagged at 4.67% [E60] and a complete absence of shareholder return via a 0.00% dividend yield [E4].
